staging.stg_social_media__account_histor.statement: Account timezone values require no deterministic trimming or casing correction before applying the deletion rule.
staging.stg_social_media__account_histor.alternative: The general staging quality actions require automatically fixing "casing, whitespace trimming" and "standardize valid IANA timezones when pattern matches".
staging.stg_social_media__account_histor.reason: Correctable timezone values would otherwise cause entire account records to be discarded.

staging.stg_social_media__account_histor.statement: All non-null account timestamp and boolean values are directly castable to their declared output types.
staging.stg_social_media__account_histor.reason: An invalid value could prevent the staging SQL and pipeline from executing.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.statement: Twitter screen names containing harmful characters may be retained if removing those characters produces a nonempty name.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.alternative: The description says "rows with NULL/blank or harmful characters are removed", which could require testing harmful characters in the original value.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.reason: The interpretation determines whether potentially unsafe source records survive staging.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.statement: All non-null Twitter profile timestamp and boolean fields used in direct casts are castable to the declared types.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.reason: Malformed source values would make execution fail rather than produce cleaned profiles.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.statement: A Twitter URL with a valid-looking prefix remains acceptable even when the rest of the value is not a valid URL.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.alternative: The staging quality documentation describes nullifying an "optional URL fails regex", which may mean validating the whole field rather than a prefix.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_user_h.reason: The unanchored ending can retain malformed optional URL values.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.statement: Organic report account_id identifies the Twitter user whose profile should enrich the tweet.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.evidence_of_dependence: left join users u on u.id = o.account_id and u.row_num = 1
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.alternative: The material index also exposes raw.tweet.user_id and raw.tweet.account_id; tweet.user_id could be the required profile join key.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: Using an account identifier as a user identifier can leave most profiles missing or attach the wrong users.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.statement: raw.tweet.full_test contains the tweet text referred to as full_text in the contract.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.alternative: The contract explicitly says "Tweet text joined from raw.tweet.full_text", while the material index lists only full_test.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: The implementation resolves a schema discrepancy without establishing the substitute field's meaning.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.statement: Each tweet identifier has at most one matching row in raw.tweet after conversion to BIGINT.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.evidence_of_dependence: left join tweets t on try_cast(o.organic_tweet_id as bigint) = t.tweet_id
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: Duplicate matches would multiply report rows and their downstream metrics.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.statement: The most recently synced Twitter profile is the intended profile for every report date, and no conflicting profiles tie at that sync time.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.alternative: The source is named twitter_user_history and reports contain date; the contract says only that user attributes are "joined from raw.twitter_user_history" without defining latest versus historical selection.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: Profile attribution can change across historical reports or become nondeterministic on ties.

staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.statement: The organic tweet output should strip disallowed characters from raw user screen names rather than preserve the joined source value.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.alternative: This model's screen_name description says "From raw.twitter_user_history.screen_name"; the explicit screen-name cleaning rules are specified separately for stg_social_media__twitter_user_history.
staging.stg_social_media__twitter_organi.reason: This changes the reported identity text and can create empty names without the profile model's row filtering.

staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.statement: Facebook staging impressions should use the maximum lifetime metric rather than the specified staging default of zero.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.evidence_of_dependence: max(post_impressions) as impressions ... coalesce(pm.impressions, 0)::bigint as impressions
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.alternative: The contract defines impressions as "Default 0 in staging" and lists only post history and page data as this model's source tables.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.reason: This introduces an additional source and changes a core performance metric for matched posts.

staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.statement: Every qualifying Facebook post has at most one row in raw.facebook_pages_post_history.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.alternative: The source includes updated_time and is named post_history, so multiple versions may require selecting a version.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.reason: Repeated versions would produce duplicate posts and potentially retain outdated visibility states.

staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.statement: Facebook post created_time and the numeric and boolean fields directly cast by this query contain only compatible values.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.reason: An incompatible source value could abort the model rather than be corrected or nullified.

staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.statement: The latest synced Facebook page record is the intended page metadata for all posts, regardless of deletion status.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.evidence_of_dependence: partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last ... pg.row_num = 1
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.alternative: raw.facebook_pages_page_data includes _fivetran_deleted, which is not consulted when selecting page metadata.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.reason: Deleted or historically inappropriate page versions could supply names and follower counts.

staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.statement: A Facebook post with a null is_hidden value should count as visible.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.alternative: The contract describes the model as "Published, visible Facebook posts" but does not define whether unknown visibility qualifies.
staging.stg_social_media__facebook_posts.reason: This determines whether posts with unknown visibility enter reporting.

staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.statement: Instagram metrics should select the first non-null media-specific field in a fixed priority order independent of the post's media_type.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.alternative: The contract refers to normalized "mi.impressions" and other normalized metrics without defining this priority; the inspected rows contain simultaneous non-null carousel, story, photo/video, and reel metrics.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.reason: The chosen priority can select the wrong metric family for most non-carousel posts.

staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.statement: Each media identifier has at most one matching Instagram insights row across all source_relation values.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.evidence_of_dependence: left join insights i on m.id = i.id
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.alternative: The insights table exposes both source_relation and _fivetran_id, but neither participates in the join or deduplication.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.reason: Multiple matches would multiply posts and metrics.

staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.statement: Each qualifying Instagram media identifier occurs only once in media history.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.alternative: The history source includes _fivetran_id and _fivetran_synced, but no media-version selection is performed.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.reason: Multiple historical versions would create duplicate post outputs.

staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.statement: Instagram media user_id and user-history id identify accounts in the same identifier namespace.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.evidence_of_dependence: left join users u on m.user_id = u.id

staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.reason: A namespace mismatch would remove account enrichment from otherwise valid posts.

staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.statement: The latest synced Instagram user record supplies the intended account metadata for every historical media post.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.evidence_of_dependence: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.alternative: The contract requests account details "from user history" but does not specify latest rather than post-time values.
staging.stg_social_media__instagram_post.reason: Account names, follower counts, and media counts can differ materially across versions.

staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.statement: LinkedIn organization-post identifiers can be matched literally to history and content identifiers without reconciling share and ugcPost URNs.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.alternative: The samples show organization-post IDs beginning "urn:li:share:" and history IDs beginning "urn:li:ugcPost:"; the implemented replacement leaves the identifier unchanged.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.reason: Unreconciled identifier forms could leave messages and creation timestamps missing across many posts.

staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.statement: Each LinkedIn post has at most one matching UGC history row.

staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.alternative: The source is a history table with last_modified_time and _fivetran_synced, but the query selects no single version.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.reason: Multiple versions would duplicate posts and produce conflicting messages or timestamps.

staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.statement: Each LinkedIn post has at most one matching post-content row.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.evidence_of_dependence: left join raw.linkedin_pages_post_content pc on pc.post_id = regexp_replace(o.ugc_post_id, '^urn:li:share:', 'urn:li:share:')
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.alternative: The content source includes media_id and _fivetran_id, which could distinguish multiple content items for one post.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.reason: A post with multiple content items would be emitted multiple times.

staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.statement: LinkedIn post_message should prefer article_title, then media_title, and use commentary only as a fallback.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.alternative: The contract lists post_message without defining this priority; the available history source contains commentary, which could instead be the post message.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.reason: The priority can replace the actual post commentary with a content title.

staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.statement: LinkedIn organization-post records with null organization identifiers should be deleted from staging.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.alternative: The contract declares organization_id as VARCHAR without a not_null constraint or delete_row rule.
staging.stg_social_media__linkedin_posts.reason: This adds an undocumented row-exclusion rule.

staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.statement: The maximum channel_subscribers across all YouTube channel-basic records is the intended subscriber count for every video on that channel.
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.evidence_of_dependence: select channel_id, max(channel_subscribers) as channel_subscribers ... group by channel_id
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.alternative: The channel-basic source includes date, while the contract specifies only "COALESCE(channel_info.channel_subscribers, 0)" and does not define maximum-over-time selection.
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.reason: A historical maximum can systematically overstate subscriber counts.

staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.statement: All YouTube publication timestamps and numeric metric values used by the query are compatible with its casts and arithmetic.
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.reason: Malformed values could prevent pipeline execution.

staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.statement: Each qualifying YouTube video identifier occurs only once in raw.youtube_video.
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.reason: Duplicate source identifiers would produce duplicate videos and metrics.

staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.statement: A missing YouTube channel title should produce the literal page_name 'Unknown Channel'.
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.alternative: The contract declares page_name as VARCHAR but provides no default or correction rule for it.
staging.stg_social_media__youtube_videos.reason: This changes only the labeling of records with missing titles.

intermediate.social_media_reporting__twi.statement: The earliest tweet_created_at in each Twitter group equals the earliest report date required for created_timestamp.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__twi.alternative: The contract specifies "created_timestamp: earliest date in the group"; staging exposes date separately from tweet_created_at.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__twi.reason: Tweet publication time and report date can differ, changing timestamps and downstream date-based reporting.

intermediate.social_media_reporting__twi.statement: Twitter screen_name, user_name, and account_id contain no whitespace-only values that must be treated as missing when choosing page_name.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__twi.alternative: The contract requires the "first non-blank" candidate and says "blank strings treated as missing"; whitespace-only strings could therefore require a trimmed emptiness check without trimming the retained value.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__twi.reason: Whitespace-only candidates can suppress valid fallback names and produce unusable canonical URLs.

intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.statement: LinkedIn interaction metrics can be treated as absent for every staging record and therefore replaced with constant zeros.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.evidence_of_dependence: coalesce(0, 0)::integer as clicks, 0::integer as impressions, 0::integer as likes, 0::integer as shares, 0::integer as comments
intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.alternative: The reporting contract says metrics are "set to 0 when null; integers are otherwise preserved", although the minimal staging schema does not declare these metrics.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.reason: This resolves a contract inconsistency by discarding any possibility of nonzero LinkedIn performance.

intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.statement: A positive source engagement_rate is unavailable for every LinkedIn staging record, so its specified precedence requires no implementation.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.evidence_of_dependence: case when impressions > 0 then (clicks + likes + comments + shares)::double / impressions else 0.0 end as calculated_engagement_rate
intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.alternative: The reporting contract requires "if the source engagement_rate is positive, use it", while the staging column list does not include engagement_rate.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__lin.reason: If source rates are intended to be supplied, the omitted branch changes all positive-rate records.

intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.statement: Facebook staging impressions always fit within the INTEGER range required by the reporting cast.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.alternative: The staging contract declares impressions as BIGINT, whereas the reporting contract declares INTEGER.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.reason: An out-of-range staging value would abort execution rather than produce the reporting table.

intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.statement: Facebook impressions never contain negative values for which the contract requires division rather than a zero engagement rate.
intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.evidence_of_dependence: case when impressions > 0 then shares::double / impressions else 0.0 end as engagement_rate
intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.alternative: The business logic says "engagement_rate is 0.0 when impressions are 0; otherwise" divide, although the denominator column description instead says "when greater than 0".
intermediate.social_media_reporting__fac.reason: Negative values expose a difference between the implemented guard and one explicit contract definition.

marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.statement: Daily aggregated clicks plus likes, shares, and comments never exceed aggregated impressions when impressions are positive.
marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.evidence_of_dependence: case when impressions > 0 then (clicks + likes + shares + comments)::double / impressions else 0.0 end as engagement_rate
marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.alternative: The daily contract requires "engagement_rate BETWEEN 0 AND 1", while the YouTube contract defines both clicks and impressions as views and allows additional interactions.
marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: Groups exceeding this bound would violate the declared validation test despite implementing the stated ratio.

marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.statement: Records without created_timestamp should be excluded before daily aggregation and date-spine construction.
marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.evidence_of_dependence:
from platform_posts
    where created_timestamp is not null
marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.alternative: The daily business logic says to ingest all five models and normalize their dates without an explicit missing-date filter, while its output day has a not_null test.
marts.social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: The choice affects whether undated activity participates in normalization and whether platforms with only undated activity appear.

marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.statement: Every recently dated intermediate record has non-null page_id and post_id.
marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.alternative: The rollup declares not_null tests for both identifiers, but Facebook permits null page_id and Twitter and YouTube also permit null page_id.
marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.reason: The rollup does not exclude or repair missing identifiers, so upstream nulls can violate its output contract.

marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.statement: The rollup's recent-data windows permit future-dated posts without an upper date boundary.
marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.evidence_of_dependence: created_timestamp >= current_date - interval '4 years' ... created_timestamp >= current_date - interval '2 years'
marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.alternative: The contract says "keep the last 4 years" and "keep the last 2 years", which could instead mean a window ending at the current date.
marts.social_media_reporting__rollup_rep.reason: Future-dated records would enter the rollup and alter its rankings under this interpretation.

marts.social_media_reporting__retention_.statement: Pages with null page_id should be removed before creating retention cohorts.
marts.social_media_reporting__retention_.evidence_of_dependence:
from page_activity
    where page_id is not null
marts.social_media_reporting__retention_.alternative: The retention contract says to "only keep rows where created_timestamp is present" and defines cohorts "For each (page_id, platform)" without an identifier exclusion.
marts.social_media_reporting__retention_.reason: Removing null identifiers can eliminate cohort weeks that the documented grouping would otherwise emit.

marts.social_media_reporting__ctr_by_pla.statement: Records without created_timestamp should be excluded entirely from monthly CTR reporting.
marts.social_media_reporting__ctr_by_pla.evidence_of_dependence:
from platform_posts
    where created_timestamp is not null
marts.social_media_reporting__ctr_by_pla.alternative: The business logic says "Union all posts" and "posts_count: number of rows (union-all, no de-duplication)", although the month column also has a not_null test.
marts.social_media_reporting__ctr_by_pla.reason: This resolves an undocumented missing-date policy by dropping records and their metrics.

stg_social_media__twitter_organic_tweets.problem: Raw screen names are modified even though this staging model specifies passing screen_name through from raw user history.
stg_social_media__twitter_organic_tweets.reason: This changes downstream page-name selection and canonical URLs rather than merely enriching the records.

stg_social_media__twitter_organic_tweets.evidence_in_work: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
stg_social_media__twitter_organic_tweets.reason: No temporal or deduplication policy is specified, and the choice can change profile attribution.

stg_social_media__twitter_organic_tweets.reason: Multiple tweet records per ID would multiply performance rows and later summed metrics.

stg_social_media__facebook_posts.evidence_in_work: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... pg.row_num = 1

stg_social_media__instagram_posts.problem: Selecting the latest user-history row introduces an undocumented current-profile enrichment policy.
stg_social_media__instagram_posts.evidence_in_work: row_number() over (partition by id order by _fivetran_synced desc nulls last) ... u.row_num = 1
stg_social_media__instagram_posts.reason: Follower counts and follower-based engagement can differ substantially between current and posting-time profiles.

social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_re.problem: Whitespace-only names are not treated as blank and account_id is not checked for blankness.
social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_re.source: choose the first non-blank among screen_name, user_name, then account_id as text (blank strings treated as missing)
social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_re.reason: Whitespace candidates can win lexicographic selection and produce invalid-looking page names and URLs.

social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_re.problem: Page names and URLs may fall back to reporting account IDs because upstream user enrichment joins incompatible account and user identifiers.
social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_re.source: raw.tweet includes user_id; raw.twitter_user_history includes id
social_media_reporting__twitter_posts_re.reason: Incorrect author attribution propagates into canonical tweet URLs.

social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.problem: Impressions are read from the staging impressions field rather than explicitly mirroring source clicks as required.
social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.source: clicks and impressions: both set to the video's views; views come from the source clicks field
social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.reason: Current staging makes the fields equal, but the intermediate transformation does not independently enforce its specified mapping.

social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.problem: views_per_subscriber inherits an unspecified historical-maximum subscriber denominator.
social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.evidence_in_work: case when channel_subscribers > 0 then clicks::double / channel_subscribers
social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.source: views_per_subscriber: clicks divided by channel_subscribers when subscribers > 0
social_media_reporting__youtube_videos_r.reason: The ratio can be understated if staging's maximum subscriber count exceeds the relevant snapshot.

social_media_reporting__rollup_report.problem: Twitter rows can be assigned the wrong date or excluded entirely because their upstream timestamp uses tweet_created_at instead of earliest report date.
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.evidence_in_work: where created_timestamp is not null ... created_timestamp >= current_date - interval '2 years'
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.source: Twitter created_timestamp: earliest date in the group
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.reason: This affects platform coverage, display ordering, recent-window filtering, and daily rankings.

social_media_reporting__rollup_report.problem: Facebook impressions, quality scores, and engagement rates inherit lifetime impressions that contradict the staging zero-impressions requirement.
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.evidence_in_work: when 'facebook' then case when impressions > 0 then 75 else 50 end
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.source: Facebook staging impressions: Default 0 in staging.
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.reason: The incorrect upstream denominator also changes cross-platform rankings.

social_media_reporting__rollup_report.problem: Instagram metrics and rankings inherit unverified cross-media-family coalescing and possible insight-join fanout.
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.evidence_in_work: from intermediate.social_media_reporting__instagram_posts_reporting; row_number() ... order by impressions desc
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.source: raw.instagram_business_media_insights contains media-family-specific metrics and source_relation
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.reason: Incorrect metrics or duplicated enrichment rows affect totals, scores, and rank positions.

social_media_reporting__rollup_report.problem: LinkedIn is absent because association records do not match history timestamps, not because the available 2023 history is outside the four-year window.
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.reason: A platform-wide coverage gap remains unresolved upstream.

social_media_reporting__rollup_report.problem: The rollup does not enforce its non-null page_id and post_id tests even though several upstream models explicitly allow null identifiers.
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.source: rollup page_id and post_id: tests: not_null
social_media_reporting__rollup_report.reason: Rows with valid timestamps but missing identifiers can violate the output contract.

social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.problem: Twitter daily buckets and spine bounds inherit the wrong timestamp definition and potentially null timestamps from failed enrichment.
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.evidence_in_work: cast(created_timestamp as date) as day; where created_timestamp is not null
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.source: Twitter created_timestamp: earliest date in the group
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: Activity can move to the wrong day or disappear before aggregation and spine construction.

social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.problem: Facebook daily impressions and rates inherit lifetime metrics despite the staging requirement to use zero impressions.
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.source: Facebook staging impressions: Default 0 in staging.
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: Facebook aggregate denominators and both reported rates would change.

social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.problem: Instagram daily sums and post counts inherit media-family misselection and possible insight-join multiplication.
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.evidence_in_work: count(*)::bigint as posts_count; sum(clicks)::hugeint as clicks
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.source: raw.instagram_business_media_insights contains separate media-family metrics and source_relation
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: These upstream issues affect aggregate counts and most KPI values.

social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.problem: LinkedIn daily activity is missing because upstream history identifiers do not match staged associations.
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.source: raw.linkedin_pages_ugc_post_history includes created_time; LinkedIn reporting retains the last 4 years
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: Without LinkedIn normalized rows, neither activity aggregates nor a platform date spine can be produced.

social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.problem: The unbounded engagement formula can violate the declared zero-to-one rate tests.
social_media_reporting__daily_kpis.reason: The formula itself is specified, but YouTube clicks equal impressions, so positive interactions can make the test impossible without resolving the contract inconsistency.

social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.problem: Twitter cohort weeks and weekly activity use upstream tweet-created timestamps rather than earliest performance dates.
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.source: Twitter created_timestamp: earliest date in the group
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.reason: Incorrect or null timestamps change cohort assignment, observed activity, and retention numerators.

social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.problem: LinkedIn cohorts are entirely absent because staged association records never receive matching history timestamps.
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.evidence_in_work: from intermediate.social_media_reporting__linkedin_posts_reporting where created_timestamp is not null
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.source: LinkedIn reporting: created_timestamp ... within the last 4 years
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.reason: The join-coverage issue eliminates all LinkedIn retention observations despite available in-window history.

social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.problem: Null page identifiers are removed before cohort formation although the input instructions only explicitly filter missing timestamps.
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.evidence_in_work: from page_activity where page_id is not null
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.source: Union page activity from the five source models; only keep rows where created_timestamp is present.
social_media_reporting__retention_kpis.reason: Distinct page counts normally ignore nulls, but this extra filter can remove otherwise observable zero-page cohort groups.

social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.problem: Twitter month buckets and row inclusion inherit the wrong timestamp source and failed tweet enrichment.
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.evidence_in_work: date_trunc('month', created_timestamp)::date as month; where created_timestamp is not null
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.source: Twitter created_timestamp: earliest date in the group
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.reason: Posts can fall into incorrect monthly groups or be excluded entirely.

social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.problem: Facebook monthly impressions and rates inherit lifetime impressions instead of the specified staging zero.
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.source: Facebook staging impressions: Default 0 in staging.
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.reason: This changes the denominators and engagement measures for Facebook groups.

social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.problem: Instagram monthly metrics and post counts inherit type-agnostic insight coalescing and possible join fanout.
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.evidence_in_work: count(*)::bigint as posts_count; sum(likes)::hugeint as likes
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.source: raw.instagram_business_media_insights includes carousel_album, video_photo, story, reel metrics and source_relation
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.reason: Incorrect inputs propagate directly into monthly sums, counts, and rates.

social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.problem: LinkedIn monthly coverage is missing because upstream association/history joins do not provide timestamps.
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.source: LinkedIn reporting includes posts within the last 4 years
social_media_reporting__ctr_by_platform.reason: The entire platform is omitted rather than merely reporting zero interactions.

zuora__line_item_history.reason: A negative matched MRR would flow directly into a field with a nonnegative test.

zuora__line_item_history.statement: Every non-null current rate-plan charge mrrhome_currency value matched to a line item is nonnegative.
zuora__line_item_history.alternative: The output contract tests "charge_mrr_home_currency >= 0," while rate_plan_charge_current preserves staging values without transformation.
zuora__line_item_history.reason: A negative matched home-currency MRR would flow directly into a field with a nonnegative test.

zuora__monthly_recurring_revenue.statement: Invoice items with null service_start_day should not produce an account-month row in monthly recurring revenue.
zuora__monthly_recurring_revenue.evidence_of_dependence: The month_spine and classified_items CTEs both use `WHERE service_start_day IS NOT NULL`.
zuora__monthly_recurring_revenue.alternative: The contract says to build the spine as "distinct pairs of (account_id, month of service_start_day set to the first day)" and that output "includes every (account_id, account_month) from the month spine," without excluding null dates.
zuora__monthly_recurring_revenue.reason: The additional filter removes account/null-month rows that the specified spine could retain.

zuora__line_item_enhanced.statement: Casting the staged BOOLEAN processing_type to VARCHAR preserves the '0', '1', '2', and '3' codes needed for transaction classification and discount calculation.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.evidence_of_dependence: The edit introduces `CASE CAST(ii.processing_type AS VARCHAR) WHEN` and `CAST(ii.processing_type AS VARCHAR) = '1'`, after inspection reports staging processing_type as BOOLEAN.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.alternative: The enhanced-model contract requires "'0'→charge, '1'→discount, '2'→prepayment, '3'→tax", whereas the staging contract declares processing_type BOOLEAN; casting a Boolean to VARCHAR produces Boolean text rather than restoring these numeric codes.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.reason: The cast can make execution succeed without recovering the codes required to classify transactions or identify discounts.

zuora__line_item_enhanced.statement: The enhanced line-item payment_method_id may come from the payment rather than the invoice-payment mapping.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.alternative: The output contract specifies "Payment method id from invoice_payments.payment_method_id; NULL if no related invoice_payment" for payment_method_id.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.reason: Different or missing payment records can change the identifier emitted under the required column name.

zuora__line_item_enhanced.statement: The enhanced line-item output is permitted to contain an additional invoice_payment_method_id column beyond the documented output columns.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.evidence_of_dependence: `ip.payment_method_id AS invoice_payment_method_id` followed by `SELECT *, row_number() ... FROM joined`
zuora__line_item_enhanced.alternative: The documented columns include payment_method_id but do not include invoice_payment_method_id.
zuora__line_item_enhanced.reason: An extra column could violate an exact-schema interpretation of the data contract.

result.md.statement: Unparsable invoice and invoice-item fields may universally be converted to NULL even where the contract specifies an ordinary CAST rather than TRY_CAST.
result.md.evidence_of_dependence: “非关键不可解析值转为 NULL” and “类型不匹配且不可安全解析的数据留下 NULL，不额外推断。”
result.md.alternative: The contract distinguishes safe conversions from ordinary casts: invoice.posted_date specifies "cast(posted_date as TIMESTAMP)", invoice.amount specifies an empty-string check followed by "cast(amount as DOUBLE)", and invoice_item.updated_date specifies "cast(updated_date as TIMESTAMP)".
result.md.reason: A blanket nullification policy changes the specified treatment of malformed values and can conceal data-quality failures.

coverage_proxy.definition: Unique method2 contract-section table names; literal output key present, including an empty list. Schema prefix removed, lowercase, exact match. Not actual write detection.

stg_zuora__account.problem: The generic identifier mapping replaces bill_to_contact_id, sold_to_contact_id, and default_payment_method_id with the account's own id.
stg_zuora__account.source: The account contract separately lists account_id, bill_to_contact_id, sold_to_contact_id, and default_payment_method_id.
stg_zuora__account.reason: These are foreign identifiers rather than aliases of the account primary key.

stg_zuora__account.problem: Comma-packed account records may be split incorrectly when text fields contain quoted commas, without any validation of field alignment.
stg_zuora__account.source: raw.zuora_account_data has a single comma-separated column header including name, notes, and additional_email_addresses.
stg_zuora__account.reason: A shifted field would corrupt many account attributes even though the SQL still executes.

stg_zuora__contact.problem: account_id is mapped from the contact id instead of the source account_id, also making the account-contact recency flag partition by the wrong entity.
stg_zuora__contact.source: contact_id source_expression: "id"; account_id is a separate source field; is_most_recent_account_contact partitions by account_id.
stg_zuora__contact.reason: This can disconnect contacts from accounts and change which contacts qualify as current.

stg_zuora__contact.problem: Phone normalization uses DuckDB regexp_replace without global replacement, so a phone with multiple punctuation characters may fail normalization.
stg_zuora__contact.source: mobile_phone uses length(regexp_replace(mobile_phone, '[^0-9]', '')) and is described as phone format standardization.
stg_zuora__contact.reason: The literal contract expression is retained, but DuckDB's default replacement behavior may not implement its stated cleaning intent.

stg_zuora__contact.problem: The account-contact recency window may resolve account_id to its newly aliased contact id rather than the intended source account_id.
stg_zuora__contact.evidence_in_work: try_cast("id" AS VARCHAR) AS account_id; row_number() over (partition by account_id ...)
stg_zuora__contact.source: is_most_recent_account_contact: row_number() over (partition by account_id order by try_cast(created_date as TIMESTAMP) desc) = 1
stg_zuora__contact.reason: DuckDB alias resolution should be checked because the projection and window reference competing meanings of the same name.

stg_zuora__invoice.problem: The generic mapping substitutes invoice id for account_id, bill_to_contact_id, sold_to_contact_id, and default_payment_method_id.
stg_zuora__invoice.evidence_in_work: pk_alias={'account_id', ... 'payment_method_id', ...}; if n in pk_alias: srcname='id'
stg_zuora__invoice.source: invoice_id source_expression: "id"; account_id and the contact and payment-method identifiers are separate columns.
stg_zuora__invoice.reason: Incorrect account attribution propagates into nearly every invoice-based analytical result.

stg_zuora__invoice.problem: Invoices with missing or unparsable created_date are deleted even though the contract explicitly permits them.
stg_zuora__invoice.evidence_in_work: try_cast(created_date AS timestamp) IS NOT NULL AND try_cast(created_date AS timestamp) <= current_timestamp
stg_zuora__invoice.source: try_cast(created_date as TIMESTAMP) is null OR (try_cast(created_date as TIMESTAMP) <= current_timestamp AND ...)
stg_zuora__invoice.reason: This removes invoices and their amounts instead of retaining them with null creation timestamps.

stg_zuora__invoice.problem: The importer may misalign invoice columns when comma-packed comments or other text contain embedded commas.
stg_zuora__invoice.source: raw.zuora_invoice_data is indexed as one comma-separated header containing comments and tax_message.
stg_zuora__invoice.reason: Unverified parsing could alter dates, amounts, and join identifiers across an entire record.

stg_zuora__invoice_item.problem: The generic primary-key fix also maps account_id, invoice_id, product_id, subscription_id, amendment_id, and rate-plan identifiers to the invoice item's own id.
stg_zuora__invoice_item.source: Only invoice_item_id has source_expression: "id"; the contract separately lists invoice_id, account_id, product_id, subscription_id, and other relationship keys.
stg_zuora__invoice_item.reason: This destroys the relationships used by all line-item, billing, and revenue joins.

stg_zuora__invoice_item.problem: The observed processing_type values look like identifiers rather than processing codes, but the agent accepts their conversion to NULL without checking source record alignment.
stg_zuora__invoice_item.source: processing_type is used downstream as the codes '0', '1', '2', and '3'.
stg_zuora__invoice_item.reason: Almost all retained records lose processing semantics, which may indicate a broader source-format problem.

stg_zuora__invoice_item.problem: Casting processing_type to BOOLEAN loses codes 2 and 3 and changes 0 and 1 into values that cannot survive later VARCHAR code comparisons.
stg_zuora__invoice_item.source: The staging type is BOOLEAN, but modeling logic requires processing_type string codes '0', '1', '2', and '3'.
stg_zuora__invoice_item.reason: The contract conflict needs explicit reconciliation rather than a cast that prevents required classification.

stg_zuora__invoice_payment.problem: invoice_id, payment_id, account_id, and payment_method_id are replaced with invoice_payment id by the generic identifier mapping.
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.source: The contract separately defines invoice_payment_id, invoice_id, payment_id, account_id, and payment_method_id.
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.reason: The join table no longer links invoices to their actual payments.

stg_zuora__invoice_payment.problem: A deletion filter is added although this table's provided contract specifies no row filter.
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.evidence_in_work: Every table with deletion metadata honors deletion ... filters.append(...)
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.source: stg_zuora__invoice_payment lists columns without a row_filters section.
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.reason: This may remove records outside the specified scope, although the intended treatment of deletion metadata is ambiguous.

stg_zuora__invoice_payment.problem: Casting numeric refund_amount to BOOLEAN discards its magnitude before a downstream model describes it as an unchanged numeric amount.
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.source: staging refund_amount: BOOLEAN; int_zuora__invoice_payment_current refund_amount: BIGINT, 'numeric values are unchanged'.
stg_zuora__invoice_payment.reason: This follows one part of a conflicting contract but may lose nonzero refund amounts.

stg_zuora__payment.problem: account_id and payment_method_id are mapped from payment id rather than their actual raw fields.
stg_zuora__payment.source: payment_id source_expression: "id"; account_id and payment_method_id are distinct contract columns.
stg_zuora__payment.reason: Payments become disconnected from customer and payment-method records.

stg_zuora__payment.problem: effective_date is converted to DATE even though downstream payment-date requirements depend on the original string and its ordering.
stg_zuora__payment.source: Staging effective_date is DATE, while billing_enriched requires 'earliest effective_date string (by string order)' and enhanced payment_at is 'verbatim string'.
stg_zuora__payment.reason: The conflicting requirements are not reconciled, and timestamps or nonstandard textual representations may be lost.

stg_zuora__payment_method.problem: The payment method's account_id is replaced with its own id.
stg_zuora__payment_method.source: payment_method_id source_expression: "id"; account_id is separately defined.
stg_zuora__payment_method.reason: The staged ownership relationship is incorrect even if not used by every current mart.

stg_zuora__payment_method.problem: The generic deletion predicate accepts arbitrary non-true strings that the table-specific predicate would exclude.
stg_zuora__payment_method.reason: Invalid or empty deletion flags can change the retained scope.

stg_zuora__product.problem: Recency ordering may use raw textual updated_date rather than the projected timestamp, making latest selection depend on input date format.
stg_zuora__product.evidence_in_work: e=expr for recency flags; order by updated_date desc
stg_zuora__product.source: raw.zuora_product_data updated_date is VARCHAR; the description promises a latest snapshot indicator.
stg_zuora__product.reason: This matches the literal window expression but can select the wrong snapshot if timestamp text is not lexically sortable.

stg_zuora__product_rate_plan.problem: product_id is replaced with the product rate plan id.
stg_zuora__product_rate_plan.source: product_rate_plan_id source_expression: "id"; product_id is a separate column.

stg_zuora__product_rate_plan.problem: Latest selection may sort VARCHAR updated_date values rather than timestamps.
stg_zuora__product_rate_plan.evidence_in_work: row_number() over (partition by id order by updated_date desc) = 1
stg_zuora__product_rate_plan.reason: Different timestamp formats could produce a nonchronological latest record.

stg_zuora__rate_plan.problem: account_id, amendment_id, product_id, product_rate_plan_id, subscription_id, and contact and payment-method keys are all substituted with rate plan id.
stg_zuora__rate_plan.source: The rate plan contract separately lists these relationship identifiers.
stg_zuora__rate_plan.reason: This prevents subscription-based rate-plan enrichment and corrupts the staged relationships.

stg_zuora__rate_plan.problem: The model adds deletion filtering not stated in the provided rate-plan contract.
stg_zuora__rate_plan.source: The supplied stg_zuora__rate_plan section contains no row_filters.
stg_zuora__rate_plan.reason: The added filter may change row scope without an explicit table-specific requirement.

stg_zuora__rate_plan_charge.problem: The generic identifier mapping replaces the charge's account, subscription, product, rate-plan, amendment, contact, and payment-method references with charge id.
stg_zuora__rate_plan_charge.source: Only rate_plan_charge_id explicitly maps from id; subscription_id, product_id, rate_plan_id, and other keys are separate fields.
stg_zuora__rate_plan_charge.reason: This breaks subscription-charge matching and multiple analytical relationships.

stg_zuora__rate_plan_charge.problem: BOOLEAN casts collapse bill_cycle_day, segment, and price_increase_percentage even though downstream definitions require their numeric values.
stg_zuora__rate_plan_charge.source: int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current defines bill_cycle_day, price_increase_percentage, and segment as BIGINT while requiring unchanged values.
stg_zuora__rate_plan_charge.reason: The staging/modeling type conflict can turn distinct numeric values into indistinguishable flags.

stg_zuora__subscription.problem: account_id, bill_to_contact_id, sold_to_contact_id, and default_payment_method_id are mapped to subscription id.
stg_zuora__subscription.source: subscription_id source_expression: "id"; the account, contact, and payment-method identifiers are separate fields.
stg_zuora__subscription.reason: Subscription customer ownership and account enrichment will be incorrect.

stg_zuora__subscription.problem: The deletion predicate retains invalid flag strings that the specified equality-to-false predicate would discard.
stg_zuora__subscription.reason: Unexpected flag representations can change the included subscription population.

stg_zuora__taxation_item.problem: invoice_id, invoice_item_id, account_id, product and subscription identifiers, and other recognized foreign keys are mapped to taxation item id.
stg_zuora__taxation_item.source: taxation_item_id source_expression: "id"; invoice_id and invoice_item_id are separately defined.
stg_zuora__taxation_item.reason: Tax amounts will not aggregate onto their actual invoices.

stg_zuora__taxation_item.problem: Comma-packed taxation rows are split without CSV quoting support or field-count validation.
stg_zuora__taxation_item.source: raw.zuora_taxation_item_data is indexed as a single comma-separated header including tax_description and tax_rate_description.
stg_zuora__taxation_item.reason: Embedded commas could shift financial values and identifiers into the wrong columns.

stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.problem: account_id, invoice_id, bill_to_contact_id, sold_to_contact_id, and default_payment_method_id are replaced by credit balance adjustment id.
stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.source: The contract separately defines credit_balance_adjustment_id, invoice_id, account_id, and the contact and payment-method identifiers.
stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.reason: Credit adjustments will not attach to their intended invoices.

stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.problem: The model adds a deletion filter absent from the provided table-specific contract.
stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.evidence_in_work: Every table with deletion metadata honors deletion
stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.source: The supplied credit balance adjustment contract contains no row_filters.
stg_zuora__credit_balance_adjustment.reason: This may remove records outside the documented transformation.

stg_zuora__amendment.problem: subscription_id is replaced with amendment id.
stg_zuora__amendment.source: amendment_id source_expression: "id"; subscription_id is a separate field.
stg_zuora__amendment.reason: Subscription overview will fail to attach the subscription's amendments.

stg_zuora__amendment.problem: Comma-packed amendment text may be misparsed when descriptions or names include embedded commas.
stg_zuora__amendment.source: raw.zuora_amendment_data is indexed as one comma-separated header containing description and name.
stg_zuora__amendment.reason: Field shifts could change dates, status, and identifiers without causing execution errors.

stg_zuora__order.problem: The generic identifier mapping replaces account_id, contact identifiers, and default_payment_method_id with order id.
stg_zuora__order.source: raw.zuora_order_data separately contains id, account_id, bill_to_contact_id, sold_to_contact_id, and default_payment_method_id.
stg_zuora__order.reason: Distinct source relationships are overwritten even though this table is not consumed by the visible marts.

stg_zuora__refund.problem: payment_method_id is replaced with refund id.
stg_zuora__refund.source: raw.zuora_refund_data separately contains id and payment_method_id.
stg_zuora__refund.reason: The staged refund loses its actual payment-method relationship.

int_zuora__account_current.problem: The pass-through preserves corrupted contact and payment-method references from the staging generator.
int_zuora__account_current.evidence_in_work: SELECT * FROM staging.stg_zuora__account WHERE is_most_recent_record = TRUE
int_zuora__account_current.source: The model must preserve all source columns exactly.
int_zuora__account_current.reason: The filter is correct, but the current snapshot inherits incorrect foreign identifiers.

int_zuora__contact_current.problem: Filtering both flags cannot recover the real account relationship after staging replaced account_id with contact id.
int_zuora__contact_current.source: Contacts must be associated with their account_id and satisfy both source recency flags.
int_zuora__contact_current.reason: The resulting contact profile can fail every account-based mart join.

int_zuora__invoice_base.problem: The model passes through account_id values that staging incorrectly replaced with invoice id.
int_zuora__invoice_base.source: account_id: Account linked to the invoice.
int_zuora__invoice_base.reason: All account-level invoice attribution can be wrong.

int_zuora__invoice_base.problem: The input is missing invoices with null or unparsable creation timestamps because staging used a stricter filter than specified.
int_zuora__invoice_base.source: The invoice row filter allows try_cast(created_date as TIMESTAMP) is null.
int_zuora__invoice_base.reason: Invoice totals and date coverage can be understated before this model runs.

int_zuora__invoice_item_base.problem: Pass-through invoice, account, product, subscription, and rate-plan keys inherit the staging substitution of invoice item id.
int_zuora__invoice_item_base.source: Pass through all source fields unchanged.
int_zuora__invoice_item_base.reason: Every downstream enrichment using these keys can fail or misattribute records.

int_zuora__invoice_item_base.problem: The discount comparison relies on implicit BOOLEAN coercion rather than the specified string-code comparison.
int_zuora__invoice_item_base.source: When processing_type equals the string '1', derive the discount amounts.
int_zuora__invoice_item_base.reason: The staging/modeling type mismatch makes discount classification dependent on DuckDB coercion instead of preserved codes.

int_zuora__billing_enriched.problem: Grouping uses invoice_id values that staging replaced with each invoice item's id rather than its invoice reference.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.source: grain: One row per invoice_id present in most-recent invoice items.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.reason: Per-invoice item counts and aggregates are effectively grouped by the wrong entity.

int_zuora__billing_enriched.problem: The payment join uses payment_id values overwritten with invoice-payment id, while tax and credit invoice references are also overwritten.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.evidence_in_work: JOIN staging.stg_zuora__payment AS p ON ip.payment_id = p.payment_id
int_zuora__billing_enriched.source: Join invoice_payment to payment on payment_id and left join taxes and credit aggregates on invoice_id.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.reason: Payment, tax, and credit metrics can all become unmatched NULLs.

int_zuora__billing_enriched.problem: payment_methods counts invoice_payment.payment_method_id instead of the payment's payment_method_id.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.source: payment_methods: number of unique payment_method_id across linked payments.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.reason: These two source fields may differ, changing the distinct method count.

int_zuora__billing_enriched.problem: Payment date aggregates are emitted as DATE rather than the required VARCHAR values and string ordering.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.evidence_in_work: min(effective_date) AS first_payment_date, max(effective_date) AS most_recent_payment_date
int_zuora__billing_enriched.source: first_payment_date and most_recent_payment_date: VARCHAR; effective_date string ordered by string order.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.reason: The output type is wrong, and noncanonical source dates may have different extrema.

int_zuora__billing_enriched.problem: Discount aggregation tests a staged BOOLEAN against string '1', while the observed source processing values were mostly identifier-like and became NULL.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.evidence_in_work: sum(CASE WHEN processing_type = '1' THEN ... ELSE 0 END)
int_zuora__billing_enriched.source: discount_charges uses processing_type equals '1' with a string compare.
int_zuora__billing_enriched.reason: A successful aggregate does not establish that actual discount records were classified.

int_zuora__transactions_grouped.problem: Account grouping and invoice-item matching use identifiers overwritten by staging's generic id mapping.
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.evidence_in_work: LEFT JOIN item_counts ic USING (invoice_id); GROUP BY account_id
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.source: grain: One row per account_id per date_day; item counts join to invoices by invoice_id.
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.reason: Daily rows can be grouped under invoice ids and have missing item counts.

int_zuora__transactions_grouped.problem: Invoices with null invoice_date are explicitly excluded even though the business logic does not specify that filter.
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.source: Group by account_id and the four time buckets; keep only records flagged as most recent.
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.reason: This changes intermediate row scope and drops associated financial amounts, although a not-null test suggests an unresolved contract tension.

int_zuora__transactions_grouped.problem: The stricter upstream creation-date filter removes otherwise permitted invoices from daily totals.
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.source: The staging invoice filter allows null try_cast(created_date as TIMESTAMP).
int_zuora__transactions_grouped.reason: Transactions with valid invoice dates but missing creation dates will be omitted.

int_zuora__transaction_date_spine.problem: Date bounds may be shortened because upstream staging wrongly excludes invoices with missing or unparsable created_date.
int_zuora__transaction_date_spine.evidence_in_work: SELECT min(CAST(invoice_date AS DATE)), max(CAST(invoice_date AS DATE)) FROM staging.stg_zuora__invoice
int_zuora__transaction_date_spine.source: Bounds must use all most-recent staging invoices, including those allowed by the null-created-date row filter.
int_zuora__transaction_date_spine.reason: If an excluded invoice supplies an endpoint, dates and the sequential index change.

int_zuora__mrr_date_spine.problem: The required ascending output order is not explicitly enforced.
int_zuora__mrr_date_spine.evidence_in_work: row_number() OVER (ORDER BY date_day) AS date_index FROM days
int_zuora__mrr_date_spine.source: The output has one unique row per date_day, ordered ascending.
int_zuora__mrr_date_spine.reason: Ordering inside a window defines index assignment but does not guarantee final result order.

int_zuora__payment_current.problem: The pass-through inherits incorrect account and payment-method identifiers from staging.
int_zuora__payment_current.source: account_id: Owning account ID; payment_method_id: Payment method ID.
int_zuora__payment_current.reason: Downstream payment-method and customer enrichment can fail.

int_zuora__payment_method_current.problem: The staged account_id copied into this table is the payment method's own id rather than its owner account.
int_zuora__payment_method_current.reason: The current snapshot preserves an invalid ownership relationship.

int_zuora__amendment_current.problem: subscription_id is inherited from staging as amendment id rather than the actual subscription reference.
int_zuora__amendment_current.reason: Subscription-level amendment joins will miss their intended records.

int_zuora__product_rate_plan_current.problem: product_id is inherited from staging as product rate plan id instead of its actual product reference.
int_zuora__product_rate_plan_current.reason: The current table exposes a corrupted product relationship.

int_zuora__rate_plan_current.problem: The current table inherits subscription_id and other foreign keys overwritten with rate plan id.
int_zuora__rate_plan_current.source: subscription_id: Subscription identifier; values and data types must be preserved from staging.
int_zuora__rate_plan_current.reason: Subscription-based plan enrichment will not find the intended rate plans.

int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current.problem: The current snapshot inherits subscription_id and other relationship keys replaced by rate plan charge id.
int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current.source: subscription_id: Subscription ID; account_id: Account owning the charge.
int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current.reason: Subscription-charge enrichment is disconnected from the correct entities.

int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current.problem: Numeric segment, bill-cycle-day, and percentage fields remain BOOLEAN despite the model's listed BIGINT output types.
int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current.source: bill_cycle_day, price_increase_percentage, and segment: BIGINT; no transformations or casts.
int_zuora__rate_plan_charge_current.reason: The conflicting contract sections are unresolved and downstream charge_segment has the wrong type.

int_zuora__subscription_current.problem: The current subscription's account_id is inherited as subscription id rather than the actual account reference.
int_zuora__subscription_current.reason: Account attribution and customer enrichment for subscriptions can fail.

int_zuora__invoice_payment_current.problem: The current mapping table inherits invoice_id, payment_id, and payment_method_id overwritten with invoice-payment id.
int_zuora__invoice_payment_current.source: invoice_id: Invoice identifier; payment_id: Payment identifier; payment_method_id: Payment method identifier.
int_zuora__invoice_payment_current.reason: It no longer represents the invoice-payment relationships needed by marts.

int_zuora__invoice_payment_current.problem: refund_amount remains BOOLEAN rather than the listed BIGINT numeric amount.
int_zuora__invoice_payment_current.source: refund_amount data_type: BIGINT; 'numeric values are unchanged'.
int_zuora__invoice_payment_current.reason: The unresolved staging/modeling type conflict may discard refund magnitude.

zuora__account_overview.problem: Account joins use contact and invoice account_id values overwritten with each record's own id upstream.
zuora__account_overview.evidence_in_work: LEFT JOIN ... contact_current AS c ON a.account_id = c.account_id; LEFT JOIN per_invoice AS pi ON a.account_id = pi.account_id
zuora__account_overview.source: Combine current account fields, current contact fields, invoice aggregates, and invoice item counts by account_id.
zuora__account_overview.reason: Most profile and financial enrichment may be NULL despite existing related source records.

zuora__account_overview.problem: items_by_account uses an inner join, so accounts with invoices but no matching items receive NULL rather than the required zero item count.
zuora__account_overview.evidence_in_work: JOIN intermediate.int_zuora__invoice_item_base AS ii ON inv.invoice_id = ii.invoice_id
zuora__account_overview.source: If an account has invoices but none have items, the count is 0.
zuora__account_overview.reason: This violates an explicit distinction between no invoices and invoices without items.

zuora__account_overview.problem: Account credit balance, MRR, and auto-pay fields are cast to VARCHAR despite the explicit no-casting pass-through rule.
